subject.title: [Feature]: Optimization for Dockerfile.sandbox-common # add retries and fix-missings for apt-get

question: Should the sandbox Dockerfile fix be retry-only, or should OpenClaw intentionally accept `--fix-missing` partial-install semantics for these images?
rationale: `Acquire::Retries` directly addresses transient APT fetch failures, while `--fix-missing` can allow requested sandbox packages to be held back after retrieval or integrity failures; that changes the build contract and needs maintainer intent.

options.title: Use retry-only APT installs
options.body: Keep `Acquire::Retries=5` for network resilience and remove `--fix-missing` so required sandbox tools still fail closed after retries.

options.title: Accept partial-install behavior
options.body: Keep `--fix-missing` only if maintainers intentionally want builds to proceed after missing packages and require package-presence verification or documentation for that contract.

options.title: Replace the linked branch
options.body: If the linked PR is not revised with proof, keep this issue open and use a narrower retry-only replacement as the landing path.

recommendation.title: Use retry-only APT installs
recommendation.body: Keep `Acquire::Retries=5` for network resilience and remove `--fix-missing` so required sandbox tools still fail closed after retries.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent Docker cache and install-smoke work makes this the best available owner for retry behavior versus package-install semantics.
